input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment for three years expressly "without reduction or termination rights". That is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT: it is multi-year, has no reduction right, no exit, and no true-up mechanic, so it fails every fallback element. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges that Customer has made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1's Order Form fee construct. Because the commitment can be deleted without collateral rewrites (§§ 7.1 and 12.3 already support a pay-for-what-you-order model), we replace § 2.1 with the preferred position: no minimum purchase or volume commitment and payment only for usage or ordered Services.

proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum and confirm fees are payable only for usage or ordered Services.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a multi-year take-or-pay commitment with no reduction or termination right, and it contradicts § 12.3's confirmation that we have given no minimum-volume commitment. We have replaced § 2.1 with our preferred position that there is no minimum commitment and we pay only for usage or ordered Services; if a commitment is essential, our fallback is one limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
